name: Sodium alginate
short: Reflux trials of alginate products (other ingredients not stated): adverse events and withdrawals no different from placebo or antacids, or for alginate plus PPI vs PPI alone. Event types not given.
text: A 2020 meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials of alginate-based formulations in people with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease found that the risk of adverse events and of treatment withdrawal did not differ between alginates and placebo or antacids, or between alginate added to a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) and the PPI alone, and concluded that the risk of adverse events with alginates is no greater than that of placebo or PPIs. The abstract does not list the formulations' other ingredients or say which adverse events occurred, so these data are on alginate products generally, not sodium alginate on its own. In a 28-day randomized trial in 48 people whose reflux symptoms persisted on PPI treatment, two alginate products each taken with a PPI had adverse event rates of 16.67% and 8.33% (p = 0.66); the abstract does not describe the events and there was no alginate-free comparison group. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
